, nor do you fear, it means:
h
Do not fear
Pharaoh and his soldiers overtaking you from behind, and
h
do not fear
drowning in front of you or being in the mud. And in a similar manner to what we said in the interpretation of that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Do not fear being overtaken
, nor do you fear, he said:
h
Do not fear
from the people of Pharaoh being overtaken, nor do you fear drowning in the sea.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
Do not fear being overtaken
, nor do you fear. He said:
h
Do not fear
that Pharaoh will overtake you after you, nor do you fear drowning before you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said:
m: The companions of Moses said: This is Pharaoh who has caught up with us, and this is the sea that has covered us, so God revealed:
h
Do not fear
the overtaking of the companions of Pharaoh, nor fear the sea’s mud.

c: Ahmad bin Al-Waleed Al-Ramli told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of some of his companions,
m: regarding his saying,
h
Do not fear being overtaken
, nor do you fear, he said: The mud. The reciters differed in reading his statement,
h
Do not fear overtaking
. The majority of reciters of the regions, except for Al-A’mash and Hamzah, read it as,
h
Do not fear overtaking
as a new sentence with la, as he said, “And be patient over it. We ask you for no provision.”
r
, so he raised it. Most of what came in this matter is the answer with la. Al-A’mash and Hamzah read it as,
h
Do not fear overtaking
, so they made
h
Do not fear
in the jussive mood as a responsivity, and they raised
h
Do not fear
as a new sentence, as He, the Most High, said, They will turn their backs to you, then they will not be helped.
r
(Al Imran 3:111)
, so he resumed with thumma. If he had intended with his statement,
h
Do not fear

, the jussive mood, and in it was the ya, it would have been permissible, as the rajaz poet said: Shake the trunk towards you and you will reap the harvest The reading that I like the most is the reading of la takhaf in the nominative case, because that is the more eloquent of the two languages, although the other is permissible. Some grammarians of Basra used to say: The meaning of his saying la takhaf is strike for them a path where you
h
do not fear being overtaken
. He said: And there is an omission in it, just as you say: I honored Zayd, meaning I honored him, and just as you say: And fear a Day when no soul will suffice for another soul at all
r
(Al-Baqarah 2:48-123)

, meaning it will not be sufficed in it. As for the grammarians of Kufa, they reject the omission in it except in the cases of times, because it is appropriate to say: I stood up today or in the day, but they do not permit that in the cases of nouns.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in reading his statement, Do not fear overtaking.
The majority of reciters of the regions, except for Al-A’mash and Hamzah, read it as, Do not fear overtaking as a new sentence with la, as he said, “And be patient over it.

Al-A’mash and Hamzah read it as, Do not fear overtaking, so they made Do not fear in the jussive mood as a responsivity, and they raised Do not fear as a new sentence, as He, the Most High, said, They will turn their backs to you, then they will not be helped.

If he had intended with his statement, Do not fear, the jussive mood, and in it was the ya, it would have been permissible, as the rajaz poet said: Shake the trunk towards you and you will reap the harvest The reading that I like the most is the reading of la takhaf in the nominative case, because that is the more eloquent of the two languages, although the other is permissible.

x: God Almighty says: So Moses traveled with the Children of Israel when We inspired him to travel with them. Then Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers when they crossed the sea. Then Pharaoh and his soldiers were overwhelmed by the sea, and they were all drowned.

And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them. God Almighty says: And Pharaoh led his people astray from the straight path, and took them astray, and that is because he led them on the path of the people of Hell, by ordering them to disbelieve in God and to deny His messengers. And he did not guide them. He says: And he did not lead them on the straight path, and that is because he forbade them from following God's Messenger Moses and believing in him, so they obeyed him, but he did not guide them by ordering them to do so, and they were not guided by following him.

God Almighty says: So when Moses and his people were saved from the sea, and Pharaoh's people were overwhelmed by the sea, We said to the people of Moses, O Children of Israel, We have saved you from your enemy Pharaoh and made an appointment with you on the right side of the Mount, and sent down to you manna and quails. We have already mentioned how God made an appointment with Moses and his people on the right side of the Mount. We have explained the manna and quails with the differences of those who differed about them, and we have mentioned the evidence for the correctness of the statement on that in what has passed before, so that there is no need to repeat it in this place. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, Qad anjinakum. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it, Qad anjinakum with the letter nun and the letter alif, and the rest of the other letters with it in the same way. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it, Qad anjinakum with the letter ta, and the rest of the other letters with it in the same way, except for His statement,
h
And We sent down upon you the manna and the quails

, for they agreed with the others in that and read it with the letter nun and the letter alif. In my opinion, they are two well-known readings that agree on the meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, Qad anjinakum.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it, Qad anjinakum with the letter nun and the letter alif, and the rest of the other letters with it in the same way.

The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it, Qad anjinakum with the letter ta, and the rest of the other letters with it in the same way, except for His statement, And We sent down upon you the manna and the quails, for they agreed with the others in that and read it with the letter nun and the letter alif.

x: And His statement,
h
Eat from the good things which We have provided for you
, God Almighty says to them: Eat, O Children of Israel, from the delicious things of Our provision which We have provided for you, and the lawful things which We have made permissible for you.
h
And do not transgress therein
, He says:
h
And do not transgress therein
, and do not wrong one another therein.

c: As Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And do not transgress therein
, he said: And do not wrong. And his saying,
h
My wrath will descend upon you
, means: My punishment will descend upon you.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Then My wrath will descend upon you
, meaning:
h
Then My wrath will descend upon you

. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz, Madinah, Basra and Kufa read it as fihalu ‘alaykum with a kasra on the ha’, and those who read it with a kasra on the lam. They interpreted it as meaning: My wrath is due upon you.

x: A group of the people of Kufa read it as fihalu ‘alaykum with a damma on the ha’, and they interpreted it as what we mentioned from Qatadah, that it will happen and
h
My wrath will descend upon you

The correct statement regarding this is that they are two well-known readings, each of which was recited by scholars of the Qur’an. God warned those of the Children of Israel to whom this statement was made that His punishment would befall them and descend upon them because of their disobedience to Him if they disobeyed Him, and He feared that it would be obligatory for them. So whether it was recited as occurrence or obligation, they had feared both meanings. God Almighty says: And whoever deserves My wrath, and it befalls him, has fallen, meaning he has fallen and become miserable.

c: As Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying then he has fallen means: he has become miserable.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of this.
The majority of the reciters of Hijaz, Madinah, Basra and Kufa read it as fihalu ‘alaykum with a kasra on the ha’, and those who read it with a kasra on the lam.
A group of the people of Kufa read it as fihalu ‘alaykum with a damma on the ha’, and they interpreted it as what we mentioned from Qatadah, that it will happen and My wrath will descend upon you.
Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct statement regarding this is that they are two well-known readings, each of which was recited by scholars of the Qur’an.
So whether it was recited as occurrence or obligation, they had feared both meanings.

x: And His statement, And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents, means: And indeed, I am the Possessor of forgiveness for whoever repents from his polytheism, and returns from it to faith in Me and believes, meaning: And devotes divinity to Me, and does not associate anyone with Me in his worship. And does righteousness, meaning: And performs My obligations that I have imposed upon him, and avoids my sins. Then is guided, meaning: Then he adheres to that, so he is upright and does not waste anything of it. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement, And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents from polytheism, and believes, he says: he believes in the Oneness of God, and does righteousness, he says: he performs the obligatory duties.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And I am indeed Forgiving to whoever repents from his sin
, believes in Him, and does righteousness between himself and God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar Al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ:
m: And I am Forgiving to whoever repents from polytheism and believes he says: and is sincere to God, and acts in sincerity to Him. They differed about the meaning of his saying,
h
Then he was guided

x: Some of them said: Its meaning is: He did not doubt his faith.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Then he was guided
, meaning: he did not doubt.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Then adhere to faith and righteous deeds.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Then he was guided
. He said: Then he adhered to Islam until he died upon it.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Then he became righteous.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar Al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ bin Anas,
m: h
Then he was guided
. He said: He followed the Sunnah of his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Others said: Rather, it means: He did the work.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement,
h
And he did righteousness and then was guided
, he said: He did the right thing.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: He knew the matter of his reward.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Al-Kalbi:
m: And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents from sin and believes from polytheism and does righteousness fulfills what is required of him and then is guided knows his reward, if good then good, and if evil then evil.

x: Others said: Ismail bin Musa Al-Fazari told us:

c: Omar bin Shaker told us:
m: I heard Thabit Al-Bunani say about His statement, And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance, he said: To the guardianship of the family of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: We chose the statement that we chose in this regard because guidance is steadfastness on guidance, and there is no meaning to steadfastness on it unless it is combined with faith and righteous deeds. So whoever does that and remains steadfast on it, there is no doubt about his guidance.
God Almighty says: What made you hurry? What made you hurry away from your people, O Moses, so that you went ahead of them and left them behind you, and you were not with them?
He said, 'They are on my trail.' He said, "My people are on my trail, catching up with me. "
h
And I hastened to You

, my Lord, that You might be pleased. He said, And I hastened and outran them, my Lord, so that You might be pleased with me." God Almighty said to Moses: What made you leave your people in such a hurry? Because He, glory be to Him, as we have been told, when He saved him and the Children of Israel from Pharaoh and his people, and crossed the sea with them, and counted them on the right side of the mountain, Moses hurried to his Lord, and Aaron remained among the Children of Israel, walking with them in the footsteps of Moses.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: God promised Moses, when He destroyed Pharaoh and his people and saved him and his people, thirty nights, then He completed them with ten, so the appointed time of his Lord was forty nights, in which He met him as He wished. So Moses left Aaron in charge of the Children of Israel, and with him was the Samaritan, who would follow in the footsteps of Moses to catch up with him. So when God spoke to Moses, He said to him, What made you hasten to leave your people, O Moses? He said, ‘They are on my trail,
h
and I hastened to You
, my Lord, that You may please.’

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And I hastened to You
, my Lord, that You might be pleased, he said: To please You.

x: God the Most High says: God said to Moses: O Moses, We have tested your people after you with the worship of the calf, and that was their trial after Moses. And by His saying after you He means: after your separation from them. God the Most High says: And the Samaritan led them astray. The Samaritan’s misleading of them was his calling them to worship the calf.
And his saying,
h
So Moses returned to his people
, means:
h
So Moses returned to his people
from the Children of Israel after the forty nights had passed, angry and grieved, angry at his people, saddened by what they had done after him of disbelief in God.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, angry and grieved, meaning: sad. And he said in Az-Zukhruf [verse 55], So when they angered us, meaning: they angered us. And grief has two meanings: anger and sadness.

c: Musa told me: Amr told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Angry and sad means: sad.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And when Moses returned to his people
, angry and grieved: meaning, sad about what his people had done after him.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement regrettably he said: sad.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. And His statement, He said, ‘O my people, did not your Lord promise you a good promise?’ means: Did not your Lord promise you that He is Forgiving to whoever repents, believes, and does righteousness and then is guided, and that He will promise you the right side of the Mount, and send down upon you manna and quails? That is the good promise of God to the Children of Israel, to whom Moses said: Did not your Lord promise you? And His statement, Has the covenant been prolonged with you, or did you desire that the wrath of your Lord should descend upon you? means: Has the covenant with Me, and with the beautiful blessings of God with you, and His favors with you, been prolonged, or did you desire that the wrath of your Lord should descend upon you? He says: Or did you desire that the wrath of your Lord should befall you, and that you would deserve it by your worship of the calf and your disbelief in God, so you broke your promise to Me? And their breaking their promise to Him was their devotion to the calf, and their abandonment of following in the footsteps of Moses for the appointment that God had promised them, and their saying to Aaron when he forbade them from worshipping the calf, and called them to follow in the footsteps of Moses, We will not cease to be devoted to it until Moses returns to us.
r

x: God Almighty says: The people of Moses said to Moses: We did not break our promise to you. By his promise, they meant his covenant that he had made to them.

c: As Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa H told us, and Al-Harith told us, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement My appointment, he said: My covenant, and that covenant and appointment is what we explained before. His saying, We own it, informs the Almighty about them that they admitted their error and said, We did not force ourselves to do what is right, and we did not control our affairs until we fell into the trial that we fell into. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as bi-malakna with a fatha on the mim. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as bi-malakna with a damma on the mim.

x: Some of the people of Basra read it as bi-malakna with a kasra. As for the fatha and the damma, they have the same meaning, and they are bi-qudratna and bi-qadhiratna, except that one of them is a verbal noun and the other is a noun. As for the kasra, it means the possession of something and its being the owner’s.
The interpreters also differed in their interpretation of it.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: We did not fail to fulfill our promise to you by our command.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of my uncle, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, We did not fail to keep our appointment with you by Our will, meaning: by Our command.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement by our kingdom he said: by our command.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: Others said: It means: our card.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: They said, ‘We did not fail to meet you by our own will’: meaning, by our own ability.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: They said, ‘We did not fail to meet you by our own will.’ He said: By our own will.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: We did not break your appointment because of our own desires, but we could not control ourselves.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, We did not fail to meet you by Our will, he said: He means by our own desire. He said: But three came, he said: And with them were ornaments that they had borrowed from the people of Pharaoh, and clothes.

x: All of these three statements on this matter are close in meaning, because whoever does not destroy himself, due to his desires overpowering him in what he was commanded, then it is not impossible in the language for him to say: So-and-so did this thing, and he does not control himself, and he did it, and he does it, and he does it, and he cannot bear to leave it. If that is the case, then it is the same with which of the three readings that reciter recites, because whoever breaks the meem of the word king directs the meaning of the speech to We have not failed to fulfill your promise, and we have the power to fulfill it because our souls have overcome us in the matter of it, and makes it from the saying of the speaker: This is the property of so-and-so because of what he owns of the possessions, and whoever opens it directs the meaning of the speech to something like that, except that he makes it a source from the saying of the speaker: I possessed the thing, I possess it as a possession and a kingdom, just as it is said: I overcame so-and-so, I overpowered him with overpowering and overpowering, and whoever closes it directs its meaning to We have not failed to fulfill your promise by our power and ability, meaning that we are able to prevent it, because whoever subdues something has acquired power over it.

Some people have rejected the reading of those who read it with the dammah, and said: What king was there at that time for the Children of Israel? They were only weak in Surat Ta-Ha 20:87 They said, "We did not fail to meet your appointment of our own accord, but we were burdened with some of the people's adornments,
h
so we threw them

away." Thus did the Samaritan throw away the burden. Egypt. So he ignored the meaning of the people and went far beyond what they intended. And those who read it with the dammah did not intend the meaning that this denier thought of them, but rather they intended that its meaning is: We did not break your promise because of the authority we had over ourselves that we could have turned it back from what it had done, because its desires overcame us in breaking your promise. And his saying,
h
But we carried burdens of the adornments of the people
, meaning: But we carried heavy loads and loads of the adornments of the people, meaning the adornments of the people of Pharaoh.

That is because when Moses wanted to take them by night from Egypt by God’s command to him, the Children of Israel were commanded to borrow from the goods and adornments of the people of Pharaoh, and he said, God will give you that as spoils, so they did, and they borrowed from the adornments of their women and their goods. That is what they said to Moses when he said to them, Has the covenant been prolonged upon you, or did you wish for the wrath of your Lord to descend upon you, so you broke your promise to Me? They said, We did not break your promise to you of our own accord,
h
but we carried burdens of the adornments of the people
. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
But we carried burdens of the adornments of the people
, refers to what the Children of Israel had of the adornments of the people of Pharaoh. He says: We were wronged by what we took of the adornments of our enemy.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, burdens, he said: heavy loads. And his statement, of the adornments of the people, he said: they are the ornaments that they borrowed from the people of Pharaoh, so they are the heavy loads.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: But we carried burdens he said:
m: heavy loads of the adornment of the people he said: their jewelry.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
But we carried burdens of the adornments of the people
, meaning: of the Copts’ jewelry.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement,
h
But we carried burdens of the adornments of the people

, he said: The ornaments that they borrowed and the clothing are not sins at all. If they were sins, we would have carried them, so they are not sins at all. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Meccans recited hamalna with a damma on the ha’ and a shaddah on the meem, meaning that Moses carried them that. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra and some of the Meccans recited it with a sukoon on the ha’ and the meem and a fatha on them, meaning that they carried that without anyone ordering them to carry it.

x: My interpretation of this is that they are two well-known readings with similar meanings, because the people carried it and Moses ordered them to carry it, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. And his saying,
h
So we threw them

, means: So we threw those burdens of the people’s adornment into the pit. So did the Samaritan throw in the same way? He says: Just as we threw in those burdens, so did the Samaritan throw in the soil of Gabriel’s horse’s hoof that he had with him. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
So we threw it
, he said:
h
So we threw it
. And thus did the Samaritan throw it, he did this.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
So we threw it
. He said: So we cast it. And thus did the Samaritan throw. And thus did he do.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
So we threw it
away: meaning, we cast it away.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this.
The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as bi-malakna with a fatha on the mim.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as bi-malakna with a damma on the mim.
Some of the people of Basra read it as bi-malakna with a kasra.

If that is the case, then it is the same with which of the three readings that reciter recites, because whoever breaks the meem of the word king directs the meaning of the speech to We have not failed to fulfill your promise, and we have the power to fulfill it because our souls have overcome us in the matter of it, and makes it from the saying of the speaker: This is the property of so-and-so because of what he owns of the possessions, and whoever opens it directs the meaning of the speech to something like that, except that he makes it a source from the saying of the speaker: I possessed the thing, I possess it as a possession and a kingdom, just as it is said: I overcame so-and-so, I overpowered him with overpowering and overpowering, and whoever closes it directs its meaning to We have not failed to fulfill your promise by our power and ability, meaning that we are able to prevent it, because whoever subdues something has acquired power over it.
Some people have rejected the reading of those who read it with the dammah, and said: What king was there at that time for the Children of Israel?

And those who read it with the dammah did not intend the meaning that this denier thought of them, but rather they intended that its meaning is: We did not break your promise because of the authority we had over ourselves that we could have turned it back from what it had done, because its desires overcame us in breaking your promise.
The reciters differed in their recitation of this.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Meccans recited hamalna with a damma on the ha’ and a shaddah on the meem, meaning that Moses carried them that.

The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra and some of the Meccans recited it with a sukoon on the ha’ and the meem and a fatha on them, meaning that they carried that without anyone ordering them to carry it.

x: And his saying,
h
Then he brought out for them a calf

, a body that mooed, means: So the Samaritan brought out for them from what they had thrown out and from what he had cast out, a calf, a body that mooed, and by mooing he means: the sound, which is the sound of cows. Then the scholars differed about how the Samaritan made the calf.
Some of them said: He fashioned it, then threw dust from Gabriel’s horse’s hoof into its mouth, making it pottery.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And thus did the Samaritan cast He said: God had set thirty nights for Moses, then completed them with ten. When the thirty had passed, the enemy of God, the Samaritan, said: What has befallen you has only befallen you as a punishment for the jewelry that was with you, so come. And it was jewelry that they were borrowing from the people of Pharaoh. So they set out with it and they threw it to him, and he made it into the shape of a cow. He had tied a handful of the traces of Gabriel’s horse in his turban or in his garment, so he threw it with the jewelry and the image. And he brought out for them a calf with a body that had a lowing It began to moo like a cow, and he said,
h
This is your god and the god of Moses

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: When Moses’ people were slow to return, the Samaritan said to them: He was only delayed from you because of the jewelry you have. They had borrowed jewelry from the people of Pharaoh, so they collected it and gave it to the Samaritan, who fashioned a calf from it. Then he took the handful that he had seized, from the traces of the king’s horse, and threw it into its stomach, and behold, it was a calf with a body that mooed. They said:
h
This is your god and the god of Moses
, but Moses forgot his Lord among you.

x: Others said about this:

c: Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: The Samaritan took some of the soil from the hoof of Gabriel’s horse, so Moses set out and appointed Aaron as his successor over the Children of Israel and promised them thirty nights, but God completed them with ten. Aaron said to them: O Children of Israel, the spoils are not lawful for you, and the jewelry of the Copts is only spoils, so gather them all together, dig a hole for them and bury them, and if Moses comes and makes them lawful, you will take them, otherwise it will be something that you will not eat. So they gathered that jewelry in that hole, and the Samaritan came with that handful and threw it, and God brought out from the jewelry a calf with a body that mooed, and the Children of Israel made an appointment with Moses, so they counted the night as one day, and the day as one day, and when it was twenty, the calf came out to them, and when they saw it, the Samaritan said to them,
h
This is your god and the god of Moses

, but he forgot, so they devoted themselves to it worshipping it, and it mooed and walked. And so did the Samaritan cast it, that is when Aaron said to them: Dig. For this jewelry, dig a hole and throw it in it. So they threw it, and the Samaritan threw up its dirt. And His statement,
h
And they said
h
This is your god and the god of Moses
,’ means: So the people of Moses who worshipped the calf said,
h
This is your god and the god of Moses
. And His statement,
h
And he forgot
, means: he was left behind and abandoned. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding his saying so he forgot as to who said it, who was described by it, and what its meaning was.

x: Some of them said: This is from God, report about the Samaritan, and the Samaritan is the one described by it. They said: Its meaning is that he abandoned the religion with which God sent Moses, which is Islam.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Hakim ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: God says, So he forgot: meaning he abandoned what he was upon of Islam, meaning the Samaritan.

x: Others said: Rather, this is report from God about the Samaritan, that he said to the Children of Israel, and that he described Moses as having gone to seek his Lord, but lost his place, which was this calf.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: So we threw it away, meaning the adornment of the people when we ordered the Samaritan when he took a handful of the trace of Gabriel, peace be upon him, and threw the handful on their adornment and it became a calf with a body that mooed. “
h
And they said
h
This is your god and the god of Moses
,” whom he set out to seek. But he forgot, meaning: Moses forgot, he went astray from it and was not guided to it.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He forgot means: Moses asked for this, but the road deviated from his path.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: He forgot, meaning: The Samaritan said: Moses forgot his Lord among you.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
So Moses forgot
, he said: They say that the Lord made a mistake with the calf.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: He forgot, he said: Moses forgot. The Lord made a mistake, the calf. The people of Moses say it.

c: Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: Fansai says: Moses left his god here and went looking for him.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement,
h
This is your god and the god of Moses
, but he forgot, he said: He says: So he forgot where his Lord promised him here, but he forgot.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
This is your god and the god of Moses
, but he forgot. He said: Moses forgot his Lord and missed Him, and this calf is the god of Moses.

x: What is more appropriate to interpret that statement that we mentioned about these people is that it is report from God Almighty about the Samaritan that He described Moses as having forgotten his Lord, and that his Lord whom he went to want was the calf that the Samaritan brought out, due to the consensus of the people of interpretation on it, and that it came after the mention of Moses, which is that it is report from the Samaritan about him, more likely than anything else.

God Almighty says, rebuking the worshippers of the calf, and those who said to it, This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot, and He criticized them for that, and belittled their dreams for what they did and what they did to him: Do they not see that the calf, which they claimed was their god and the god of Moses, does not speak to them, and if they spoke to it, it would not respond to them, and it is not able to harm or benefit, so how can something with this description be a god?

c: As Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa H told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, That he should not return to them a word the calf.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Do they not see that no word will return to them? He said: The calf.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: God said: Do they not see that the calf they took will not return to them in word and that it has no power to harm or benefit them?

x: And his saying,
h
And Aaron had said to them before

: He says: Aaron had said to the calf worshippers among the Children of Israel, before Moses returned to them, and what he said to them, of what God informed us about, You are only being tested by it, meaning: God only tested your faith and your adherence to your religion with this calf, which caused the lowing among them, to know by it the one among you who is sound in faith from the one who is sick in heart, who doubts his religion.

c: As Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: Aaron said to them, You were only tested by it, meaning: You were only tested by it, meaning: by the calf. And His statement,
h
And your Lord is the Most Gracious
, so follow me and obey my command. He says:
h
And your Lord is the Most Gracious

, whose blessings encompass all creation, so follow me in what I command you to do of worshipping God and abandoning the worship of the calf, and obey my command in what I command you to do of obeying God and sincerely worshipping Him.

x: And his saying, They said, ‘We will never cease to worship it,’ means: The calf worshippers from the people of Moses said: We will never cease to worship the calf, until Moses returns to us.
God Almighty says: Moses said to his brother Aaron when he finished addressing his people and reviewing them: To them, for what they had done wrong: O Aaron,
h
what prevented you
when you saw them go astray? Their religion, so they disbelieved in God and worshipped the calf. Will you not follow me?
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of what Moses blamed his brother for not following him.
Some of them said: He blamed him for not following those who obeyed him in his footsteps as he had been entrusted with.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Hakim bin Jubair, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: said, when the people said, We will not cease to be devoted to it until Moses returns to us, Aaron remained among those Muslims who followed him who did not… He was tempted, and he established those who worshipped the calf on the worship of the calf, and Aaron was afraid if he went with those with him It was said to him by Muslims that Moses said to him, You have divided the Children of Israel and have not observed my word. He is obedient and fearful.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement:
h
What prevented you
, when you saw them going astray, from following them? He said: Leave them.

x: Others said: Rather, he blamed him for not correcting the corruption of the people.
Who said that: Al-Qasim told us, he said:

c: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement, What prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following them? He said: Moses ordered Aaron to reform and not follow the path of the corruptors, so that is what he said, “that you do not follow. Did you disobey my command?” with that.

x: And his saying, He said, 'O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head.' And in this speech there is something omitted, he omitted mentioning it because the speech indicates it, which is: Then Moses took hold of his brother Aaron's beard and his head, pulling him towards him, and Aaron said, O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head. And his saying, Indeed, I feared that you would say, ‘You have divided the Children of Israel and did not observe my word,’ the scholars differed about the nature of the division between them that Aaron feared.

Some of them said: Aaron was afraid that he would lead those who obeyed him and remained in his religion in the footsteps of Moses, and leave behind the worshippers of the calf. They had said to him, We will not cease to be devoted to it until Moses returns to us. So Moses would say to him, You have divided the Children of Israel and did not observe my word, by leading a group and leaving a group behind him.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God Almighty, What prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following them? Did you disobey my command? He said, I feared that you would say, ‘You have divided the Children of Israel and did not observe my word.’ He said, I feared that some of them would follow me and some would stay behind.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: I feared that we would fight and kill each other.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: I feared that you would say, ‘You have divided the Children of Israel and have not respected my word.’ He said: We would be two groups, and some of us would kill each other until we were all gone.

x: The more correct of the two statements on this matter is the statement made by Ibn ʿAbbas, that Moses rebuked his brother Aaron for not following his command with those who followed him from the people of faith. Aaron said to him: I feared that you would say: You have divided their group, so you left some of them behind you and brought some of them. This is clear in Aaron’s statement to the al-Nas 114:O my people, you are only being tested by it, and your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command. And in the people’s response to him and their saying: We will not cease to be devoted to it until Moses returns to us. His saying,
h
And you did not observe my words
, means:
h
And you did not observe my words
and memorize them. From a man observing something, which is debating it based on his memory.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas said, And you did not observe my word, he said: You did not memorize my word.

x: God Almighty means by His saying,
h
What is the matter with you
, O Samaritan? Moses said to the Samaritan:
h
What is the matter with you
, O Samaritan, and what made you do what you did?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
What is the matter with you
, O Samaritan? He said: What is your matter? What is your affair? What is this that has brought you into what you have entered into.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: “He said:
h
What is the matter with you
, O Samaritan?” He said:
h
What is the matter with you
, O Samaritan?

x: And his saying,
h
I saw what they did not see
, means: The Samaritan said: I knew what they did not know, and it is an action from insight: meaning I became seeing and knowing with what I did.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: When Pharaoh killed the children, the mother of the Samaritan said: If you would remove him from me so that I do not see him, nor know who killed him, so she put him in a cave, and Gabriel came and put his hand in his mouth, and he began to nurse him with honey and milk, and he kept going back and forth to him until he recognized him, and from that he recognized him when he said:
h
So I took a handful from the trace of the Messenger

x: Others said: It means:
h
I saw what they did not see
. They said: It is said: I saw the thing and I saw it, just as it is said: I hastened and I hastened as I wished. It was mentioned that it means I saw.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: “He said:
h
I saw what they did not see
,” meaning the horse of Gabriel, peace be upon him. And his saying,
h
So I took a handful from the trace of the Messenger
, means: I took a handful from the trace of Gabriel’s horse. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Hakim ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: When the Children of Israel threw the ornaments of Pharaoh’s family into the fire, and they were broken, the Samaritan saw the mark of Gabriel’s horse, peace be upon him, so he took some dirt from the mark of his hoof, then he went to the fire and threw it into it. He said: Be a calf with a body that moos, so it was for affliction and tribulation.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me,
m: he told me, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: He took a handful of it from the trace of Gabriel, and threw the handful on their jewelry, and it became a calf with a body that mooed, and he said: This is your god and the god of Moses.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us
And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God,
h
So I took a handful from the trace of the Messenger

and threw it, he said: From under the hoof of Gabriel’s horse, the Samaritan threw it onto the adornment of the Children of Israel, and it descended into a calf with a body that mooed, the rustle of the wind in it, so it is its moo, and the calf is the offspring of a cow. The readers differed in the reading of these two letters. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra read it as basarat bi ma lam yabasara bih with a ya’, meaning: The Samaritan said: I saw what the Children of Israel did not see. The majority of the readers of Kufa read it as basarat bi ma lam tbasara bih with a ta’, addressing Moses, peace be upon him, and his companions, meaning: The Samaritan said to Moses: I saw what you and your companions did not see. In my opinion, they are two well-known readings. Scholars of the Qur’an recited each of them, with the meaning of each of them being correct. This is because it is possible that the Samaritan saw Gabriel, and he had what it was, because his soul told him that, or for some other reason, that the dust of his horse’s hoof that he was wearing was suitable for what he had said when he threw it into the calf. Moses did not know that, nor did his companions from the Children of Israel. Therefore, he said to Moses,
h
I saw what they did not see
, meaning I knew what they did not know. But if it is read,
h
I saw what they did not see
, with the letter ya, then there is no difficulty in that, because it is known that the Children of Israel did not know what that dust was suitable for. As for his saying,
h
So I took a handful of the Messenger’s trace
, the reciters of the regions read it with the letter Ḍād, meaning: So I took with my hand some dirt from the dirt of the Messenger’s horse’s trace.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Qatada
m: that: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Auf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he read it as fa-qadbat-qabdat with a sad.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibad, on the authority of Qatada,
m: likewise with the letter sad. Meaning: I took with my fingers some of the dirt from the traces of the Messenger’s horse. The fist among the Arabs means taking with the entire hand, and the handful means taking with the tips of the fingers. His saying,
h
So I threw it away
, means:
h
So I threw it away

. And thus my soul enticed me, means: And just as I did when I threw the handful that I had taken from the horse’s trace onto the ornament that was lit until it flowed and became a calf with a body that mooed. My soul enticed me, means: My soul made it seem good to me that it would be like this.

c: As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: And thus my soul prompted me. He said: Thus my soul prompted me.

evidence.text: The readers differed in the reading of these two letters.
The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra read it as basarat bi ma lam yabasara bih with a ya’, meaning: The Samaritan said: I saw what the Children of Israel did not see.

The majority of the readers of Kufa read it as basarat bi ma lam tbasara bih with a ta’, addressing Moses, peace be upon him, and his companions, meaning: The Samaritan said to Moses: I saw what you and your companions did not see.
But if it is read, I saw what they did not see, with the letter ya, then there is no difficulty in that, because it is known that the Children of Israel did not know what that dust was suitable for.

As for his saying, So I took a handful of the Messenger’s trace, the reciters of the regions read it with the letter Ḍād, meaning: So I took with my hand some dirt from the dirt of the Messenger’s horse’s trace.

It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Qatada that: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ibad bin Auf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he read it as fa-qadbat-qabdat with a sad.

x: God Almighty says: Moses said to the Samaritan: Go, for during your lifetime you will have the right to say: No touching, meaning no yesterday, no yesterday... to whom you have been devoted, meaning: to whom you have stayed. h

means: He encompasses all things in knowledge, so He knows them, so nothing of them is hidden from Him, and the knowledge of all of that is not difficult for Him. It is said from this: So-and-so is capable of this matter: if he is able to do it and is strong enough to do it, and he is not capable of it: if he is unable to do it, so he is not able to do it and is not strong enough to do it.
Qatada used to say about this:

He says: Thus do We inform you of the report of things that have already occurred before you, but you have not seen or witnessed them. And His statement, And We have given you from Ourselves a reminder, God the Almighty says to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: And We have given you, O Muhammad, from Ourselves a reminder by which people of reason and understanding may remember and be admonished, and it is this Qur’an that God revealed to him, making it a reminder for the worlds.

and does not believe in it or acknowledge it, then he will bear a burden

, meaning: He will come to his Lord

carrying a heavy burden, and that is a great sin.

, the Most High says: And evil will be for them on the Day of Resurrection,
h
on the Day the Trumpet is blown
. So His statement,
h
On the Day the Trumpet is blown

, is a response to the Day of Resurrection. We have already explained the meaning of blowing the Trumpet, and we have mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differ on the meaning of the Trumpet. The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is its evidence, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place before. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it as the Day when the Trumpet is blown with a ya’ and a damma on it for what the agent is not named, meaning: the Day when God commands Israfil to blow the Trumpet. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ used to read it as the Day when we blow the Trumpet with a nun, meaning: the Day when we blow the Trumpet.

What prompted him to read it this way was his request to reconcile it with his statement and we will gather the criminals, since there was no disagreement among the reciters that we will gather is with a nun.

What I chose in this reading is the day it is blown with the letter ya in the form of what its agent is not named, because that is the reading that the readers of the regions follow, because what Abu ʿAmr read had a non-corrupted form. And His statement,
h
And We shall gather the criminals that Day blue-eyed

, means, And We shall drive the people of disbelief in God that Day to the place of Resurrection, provided with provision. It was said that what is meant by blue in this place is what appears in their eyes from the intensity of thirst that will be with them when they are gathered, due to the sight of blue-eyedness. It was also said that what is meant by this is that they will be gathered blind, like what God said, And We shall gather them on the Day of Resurrection, blind (al-Isra’ 17:67).

x: The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: What is meant by crookedness is the inclination, and that is because that is what is known in the speech of the Arabs.
Is there any crookedness on earth?
You will not see any crookedness on that day.

It would be said: The meaning of that is: There are no valleys or obstacles in it that prevent the observer or the traveler from taking it in a straight path, just as today someone who takes some of its paths needs to take sometimes to the right and sometimes to the left, because of the mountains, valleys and seas in it. As for the word umt, among the Arabs, it means bending and weakness. It is heard from them: He stretched his rope until he left no bend in it, meaning a bend, and he filled his water skin until he left no bend in it. And from this is the saying of the rajaz poet: There is no attraction to his biography from the nation Meaning: from weakness and frailty. So if that is the meaning of the nation according to them, then the most correct statement in its interpretation should be neither rising nor falling, because the falling was only due to rising. So if that is the case, then the interpretation of the statement is: You do not see in it any inclination from being level, nor rising, nor falling, but it is level and smooth, as the Most High said, a flat plain.

The meaning is: There is no crookedness for them from it, because the meaning of the speech is what we mentioned, that they do not crook to it or from it, but they turn to it and come to it.
